sections.heading: FAQ

items.q: Do bina families in Toronto meet in person?
items.a: Yes. Toronto families meet every month, and classmates are introduced by age.
9am–2pm Eastern time, live, 5 days a week.

items.q: Can my child study at bina in Ontario?
items.a: Yes. Ontario's Education Act (section 21) lets a child learn at home or elsewhere instead of attending a local school, and families who choose bina homeschool under that law. bina provides the full school day: live teachers, classmates, curriculum and progress reports. You tell your school board in writing, using the letter of intent in Ontario's homeschooling policy (PPM 131), ideally before September 1 each year. [PENDING: verify against the Ontario guide] Every step is in our Ontario homeschooling guide.

items.q: Does bina follow the Ontario curriculum?
items.a: Yes, and goes further. bina uses the Ontario Curriculum as its Canadian reference, alongside England's National Curriculum and US Common Core. Each topic is taught at the earliest grade any of them teaches it, so fractions, grammar and phonics often come earlier than in Ontario schools. Levels follow age: open “Where does my child fit?” on the primary and middle school cards to see which bina level matches your child's Ontario grade.

items.q: Can we go back to a local school later?
items.a: Yes. bina is Cognia accredited and a registered Cambridge International School, so your child leaves with a school record other schools recognise. Learners finish middle school with a Cambridge-accredited record and a capstone project, ready to walk into any high school and thrive. If you move back to a local school, our Family Success team helps with the paperwork, local requirements and next steps.
